title: [leyden-dev] garding scratch (proxy) class loaders in the AOT cache
content:
Thread: garding scratch (proxy) class loaders in the AOT cache
List: leyden-dev@openjdk.org | Messages: 1+

[OP] The older CDS tech has done some work on custom class loaders. It might scale to the newer AOT tech as well. We discussed that today. Here are my thoughts on that FTR. One idea, already present in the CDS tech is this… At AOT time, we ask, "Were there custom class loaders used by the app in the training run?" And we should also demand (to start with) that these CCLs are "super simple". They are literally URL CLs, not subclassed, and not constructed with "problematic" parameters. ("Problematic" is whatever gives problems to the scheme we are trying to build!) If we find evidence of such safe-and-sane CLs, then we are willing to create them in the assembly phase. Further, we are willing to create classes loaded by them (from the JARs they mention), also if those classes are "not problematic" (in the proper sense — just as we don’t load some weird classes into the AOT cache even for the standard CLs). The result is an AOT cache where some simple URL CL, call it X0 (wait for X1…), and there are also loaded and linked classes in X0, called A,B,C. They have jl.Class mirrors that point to X0 as their loader. So far this is the same as CDS, basically, but with more optimization details. When the application runs in production, X0 and A,B,C are in the AOT cache, and A.class and the other mirrors are live in the Java heap. Those mirrors can be found by inspecting internal JDK tables.
